title: Strategic Centrality and the Emergence of Core-Periphery Networks
abstract: arXiv:2609.02357v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study a network formation game in which agents sponsor links at a linear cost in order to maximize centrality, defined as a weighted sum of walk counts with positive and weakly decreasing weights. This class includes Katz Bonacich centrality and total communicability and captures environments in which access decays with distance. Our main result is a sharp equilibrium characterization: every Nash equilibrium network is core periphery, meaning there exists a set $C$ such that every node is linked to every node in $C$, and there are no other edges. The driving force is that linking to better connected agents generates many additional short connections at once, so incentives concentrate links on a dense subset. Finally, we show that the welfare maximizing network is always either empty or complete.

translated_title: 战略中心性与核心-边缘网络的形成
translated_abstract: 我们研究了一个网络形成博弈，其中参与者以线性成本建立链接以最大化其中心性，该中心性定义为游走次数的加权和，权重为正且单调递减。这一类中心性包括Katz-Bonacich中心性和总可沟通性，并刻画了接触机会随距离衰减的环境。我们的主要结果是给出了一个精确的均衡刻画：每一个纳什均衡网络都是核心-边缘结构的，即存在一个集合 $C$，使得每个节点都与集合 $C$ 中的每个节点相连，且不存在其他边。其背后的驱动力在于，与连接更良好的参与者建立链接能够一次性产生许多额外的短路径连接，因此激励会将链接集中于一个密集的子集上。最后，我们证明福利最大化的网络总是要么为空网络，要么为完全网络。
tldr: 该论文通过策略性网络形成博弈证明：当参与者以线性成本建立链接以最大化中心性时，所有纳什均衡网络均呈现核心-边缘结构，且福利最优网络要么为空网络要么为完全网络。
en_tdlr: In a network formation game where agents pay linear link costs to maximize centrality, every Nash equilibrium network exhibits a core-periphery structure, and the welfare-maximizing network is always either empty or complete.
